references.text: Moses repeats the command to render just judgment without showing partiality, whether to the small or the great.
Prohibition against perverting justice and accepting bribes, with a command to pursue righteousness.
Warns against favoring the poor in his lawsuit, which aligns with the prohibition against lifting up the face of the poor.
Prohibition against perverting justice for the poor and against accepting bribes, for bribes blind the eyes.
A wisdom saying that it is not good to show partiality in judgment.
Warns against showing partiality, which is evil.
James warns against showing partiality based on wealth or poverty, calling it sin.
Jesus commands not to judge by outward appearance but to judge with righteous judgment.
Describes God as one who shows no partiality and accepts no bribes, an example for righteous judgment.
Job warns against showing partiality, for God will punish those who do so in secret.
